passages.text: At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the Sabbath. His disciples were hungry and began to pick the heads of grain and eat them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus walked through the grainfields on the Sabbath.
His disciples were with Him.
The disciples became hungry.
They began to pick heads of grain.
They ate the grain.
passages.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἐπορεύθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς σάββασιν διὰ τῶν σπορίμων οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπείνασαν καὶ ἤρξαντο τίλλειν στάχυας καὶ ἐσθίειν

passages.text: When the Pharisees saw this, they said to Him, “Look, Your disciples are doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath.”
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees saw Jesus and His disciples.
The Pharisees spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Look at Your disciples.”
“Your disciples are doing something on the Sabbath.”
“What they are doing is not lawful on the Sabbath.”
passages.original: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἰδόντες εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ἰδοὺ οἱ μαθηταί σου ποιοῦσιν ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν ποιεῖν ἐν σαββάτῳ

passages.text: Jesus replied, “Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
He answered their accusation.
He said, “Have you read about David?
David was hungry.
His companions were also hungry.
David did something at that time.
Have you read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε τί ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὅτε ἐπείνασεν καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: He entered the house of God, and he and his companions ate the consecrated bread, which was not lawful for them to eat, but only for the priests.
passages.sermon:
David was hungry.
His companions were also hungry.
David entered the house of God.
His companions entered with him.
David ate the consecrated bread.
His companions ate the consecrated bread.
The Law allowed only the priests to eat this bread.
It was not lawful for David to eat this bread.
It was not lawful for his companions to eat this bread.
Only the priests could eat the consecrated bread.
passages.original: πῶς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ἔφαγον ὃ οὐκ ἐξὸν ἦν αὐτῷ φαγεῖν οὐδὲ τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ εἰ μὴ τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν μόνοις

passages.text: Or haven’t you read in the Law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple break the Sabbath and yet are innocent?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He referred to the Law of Moses.
He asked if they had read the Law.
The Law says something about the priests.
The priests work in the temple on the Sabbath.
Their work breaks the Sabbath rules.
But the Law does not blame the priests.
The priests are innocent.
passages.original: Ἢ οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ἐν τῷ νόμῳ ὅτι τοῖς σάββασιν οἱ ἱερεῖς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τὸ σάββατον βεβηλοῦσιν καὶ ἀναίτιοί εἰσιν

passages.text: But I tell you that something greater than the temple is here.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said something important.
He said, “Something greater than the temple is here.”
Jesus was talking about Himself.
Jesus is greater than the temple.
The temple was very important to the Jews.
But Jesus is more important than the temple.
Jesus is here now.
passages.original: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι τοῦ ἱεροῦ μεῖζόν ἐστιν ὧδε

passages.text: If only you had known the meaning of ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned the innocent.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus referred to a teaching from God.
God said, “I desire mercy, not sacrifice.”
Jesus said, “If you understood this teaching, you would act differently.”
You would not condemn innocent people.
You would show mercy instead.
passages.original: Εἰ δὲ ἐγνώκειτε τί ἐστιν Ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν οὐκ ἂν κατεδικάσατε τοὺς ἀναιτίους

passages.text: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
passages.sermon: Jesus is the Son of Man.\r\nJesus has authority over the Sabbath.\r\nThe Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.
passages.original: κύριος γάρ ἐστιν τοῦ σαββάτου ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου

passages.text: Moving on from there, Jesus entered their synagogue, and a man with a withered hand was there. In order to accuse Jesus, they asked Him, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus left that place.
He went into their synagogue.
A man was there.
This man had a withered hand.
Some people wanted to accuse Jesus.
They asked Jesus a question.
They said, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”
passages.original: Καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτῶν καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος χεῖρα ἔχων ξηράν καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες Εἰ ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν θεραπεῦσαι ἵνα κατηγορήσωσιν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: He replied, “If one of you has a sheep and it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will he not take hold of it and lift it out?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
He asked a question.
He said, "Suppose one of you owns a sheep.
Imagine that sheep falls into a pit on the Sabbath.
Will you not take hold of the sheep?
Will you not lift it out of the pit?"
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τίς ἔσται ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος ὃς ἕξει πρόβατον ἕν καὶ ἐὰν ἐμπέσῃ τοῦτο τοῖς σάββασιν εἰς βόθυνον οὐχὶ κρατήσει αὐτὸ καὶ ἐγερεῖ

passages.text: How much more valuable is a man than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people in the synagogue.\r\nHe said that a man is much more valuable than a sheep.\r\nHe said it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.
passages.original: πόσῳ οὖν διαφέρει ἄνθρωπος προβάτου ὥστε ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν καλῶς ποιεῖν

passages.text: Then Jesus said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” So he stretched it out, and it was restored to full use, just like the other.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw a man with a withered hand.
Jesus spoke to the man.
Jesus said, “Stretch out your hand.”
The man stretched out his hand.
His hand became healthy.
His hand was just like the other hand.
passages.original: Τότε λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ Ἔκτεινόν σου τὴν χεῖρα καὶ ἐξέτεινεν καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ὑγιὴς ὡς ἡ ἄλλη

passages.text: But the Pharisees went out and plotted how they might kill Jesus.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees were religious leaders.
They went out from that place.
They made a plan against Jesus.
They wanted to kill Jesus.
passages.original: ἐξελθόντες δὲ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συμβούλιον ἔλαβον κατ’ αὐτοῦ ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν

passages.text: Aware of this, Jesus withdrew from that place. Large crowds followed Him, and He healed them all, warning them not to make Him known.
passages.sermon:
Jesus knew the Pharisees wanted to kill Him.
Jesus left that place.
Many people followed Jesus.
Jesus healed all the people who followed Him.
Jesus warned the people.
He told them not to make Him known.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς γνοὺς ἀνεχώρησεν ἐκεῖθεν καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοί καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτοὺς πάντας καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ φανερὸν αὐτὸν ποιήσωσιν

passages.text: This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah: “Here is My Servant, whom I have chosen, My beloved, in whom My soul delights. I will put My Spirit on Him, and He will proclaim justice to the nations.
passages.sermon:
God spoke through the prophet Isaiah.
God said, “Here is my Servant.
I have chosen Him.
He is my beloved.
My soul delights in Him.
I will put my Spirit on Him.
He will proclaim justice to the nations.”
passages.original: ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος Ἰδοὺ ὁ παῖς μου ὃν ᾑρέτισα ὁ ἀγαπητός μου εἰς ὃν εὐδόκησεν ἡ ψυχή μου θήσω τὸ Πνεῦμά μου ἐπ’ αὐτόν καὶ κρίσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπαγγελεῖ

passages.text: He will not quarrel or cry out; no one will hear His voice in the streets.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is gentle.
\r\nJesus does not quarrel.
\r\nJesus does not cry out.
\r\nNo one hears Jesus shouting in the streets.
passages.original: οὐκ ἐρίσει οὐδὲ κραυγάσει οὐδὲ ἀκούσει τις ἐν ταῖς πλατείαις τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: A bruised reed He will not break, and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish, till He leads justice to victory.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Servant chosen by God.
God loves Jesus.
God delights in Jesus.
God puts His Spirit on Jesus.
Jesus will proclaim justice to the nations.
Jesus will not break a bruised reed.
Jesus will not extinguish a smoldering wick.
Jesus will do this until He leads justice to victory.
passages.original: κάλαμον συντετριμμένον οὐ κατεάξει καὶ λίνον τυφόμενον οὐ σβέσει ἕως ἂν ἐκβάλῃ εἰς νῖκος τὴν κρίσιν

passages.text: In His name the nations will put their hope.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the subject.
Jesus is gentle and compassionate.
The nations are all the peoples of the world.
The nations will put their hope in Jesus.
They will trust in His name.
His name gives hope to all people.
passages.original: καὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν

passages.text: Then a demon-possessed man who was blind and mute was brought to Jesus, and He healed the man so that he could speak and see.
passages.sermon:
A man was demon-possessed.  
This man was blind.  
This man was mute.  
People brought this man to Jesus.  
Jesus healed the man.  
The man began to speak.  
The man began to see.
passages.original: Τότε προσηνέχθη αὐτῷ δαιμονιζόμενος τυφλὸς καὶ κωφός καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτόν ὥστε τὸν κωφὸν λαλεῖν καὶ βλέπειν

passages.text: The crowds were astounded and asked, “Could this be the Son of David?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus healed a demon-possessed man who was blind and mute.
The man could now speak and see.
All the crowds saw this.
The crowds were amazed.
The crowds said, “Could this man be the Son of David?”
passages.original: καὶ ἐξίσταντο πάντες οἱ ὄχλοι καὶ ἔλεγον Μήτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς Δαυίδ

passages.text: But when the Pharisees heard this, they said, “Only by Beelzebul, the prince of demons, does this man drive out demons.”
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees were religious leaders.
They heard about Jesus healing the demon-possessed man.
They spoke about Jesus.
They said, “This man drives out demons only by Beelzebul.”
Beelzebul is the prince of demons.
They claimed Jesus used the power of Beelzebul to cast out demons.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες εἶπον Οὗτος οὐκ ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια εἰ μὴ ἐν τῷ Βεελζεβοὺλ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων

passages.text: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and every city or household divided against itself will not stand.
passages.sermon:
Jesus knew what the Pharisees were thinking.
He spoke to them.
He said, “Every kingdom that is divided against itself will be destroyed.
Every city that is divided against itself will not last.
Every household that is divided against itself will fall.”
passages.original: Εἰδὼς δὲ τὰς ἐνθυμήσεις αὐτῶν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πᾶσα βασιλεία μερισθεῖσα καθ’ ἑαυτῆς ἐρημοῦται καὶ πᾶσα πόλις ἢ οἰκία μερισθεῖσα καθ’ ἑαυτῆς οὐ σταθήσεται

passages.text: If Satan drives out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then can his kingdom stand?
passages.sermon:
Satan is the ruler of demons.
If Satan drives out Satan, he acts against himself.
He becomes divided against himself.
A kingdom divided against itself cannot stand.
Satan’s kingdom cannot stand if he is divided.
passages.original: καὶ εἰ ὁ Σατανᾶς τὸν Σατανᾶν ἐκβάλλει ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν ἐμερίσθη πῶς οὖν σταθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So then, they will be your judges.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people who questioned Him.
Jesus said, "If I drive out demons by Beelzebul, tell me this.
By whom do your sons drive out demons?
Your sons also cast out demons.
Therefore, your sons will be your judges."
passages.original: Καὶ εἰ ἐγὼ ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν ἐν τίνι ἐκβάλλουσιν διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὶ κριταὶ ἔσονται ὑμῶν

passages.text: But if I drive out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to the people.
\r\nJesus has power to drive out demons.
\r\nJesus uses the Spirit of God to drive out demons.
\r\nIf Jesus drives out demons by the Spirit of God, this shows something important.
\r\nThe kingdom of God has come upon the people.
\r\nThe arrival of God's kingdom is shown by Jesus driving out demons through God's Spirit.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ ἐν Πνεύματι Θεοῦ ἐγὼ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Or again, how can anyone enter a strong man’s house and steal his possessions, unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he can plunder his house.
passages.sermon:
A strong man owns a house.
He keeps his possessions there.
No one can enter the strong man’s house and steal his possessions unless he first ties up the strong man.
If someone ties up the strong man, then he can plunder the house.
passages.original: Ἢ πῶς δύναταί τις εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἰσχυροῦ καὶ τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ ἁρπάσαι ἐὰν μὴ πρῶτον δήσῃ τὸν ἰσχυρόν καὶ τότε τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ διαρπάσει

passages.text: He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters.
passages.sermon: Jesus speaks to the people.\r\nJesus says, "Anyone who is not with Me stands against Me."\r\nAnyone who does not gather with Me scatters."
passages.original: Ὁ μὴ ὢν μετ’ ἐμοῦ κατ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν καὶ ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ’ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει

passages.text: Therefore I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to the people.
Jesus has authority to forgive sins.
Jesus says this clearly.
Every sin will be forgiven people.
Every blasphemy will be forgiven people.
But blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
passages.original: Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν πᾶσα ἁμαρτία καὶ βλασφημία ἀφεθήσεται τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ἡ δὲ τοῦ Πνεύματος βλασφημία οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται

passages.text: Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the one to come.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus is the Son of Man.
If anyone speaks against the Son of Man, God will forgive that person.
If anyone speaks against the Holy Spirit, God will not forgive that person.
God will not forgive this sin in this age.
God will not forgive this sin in the age to come.
passages.original: καὶ ὃς ἐὰν εἴπῃ λόγον κατὰ τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ ὃς δ’ ἂν εἴπῃ κατὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος τοῦ Ἁγίου οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ οὔτε ἐν τούτῳ τῷ αἰῶνι οὔτε ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι

passages.text: Make a tree good and its fruit will be good, or make a tree bad and its fruit will be bad; for a tree is known by its fruit.
passages.sermon:
A tree can be good or bad.
If you make a tree good, its fruit will be good.
If you make a tree bad, its fruit will be bad.
You can recognize a tree by its fruit.
passages.original: Ἢ ποιήσατε τὸ δένδρον καλὸν καὶ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ καλόν ἢ ποιήσατε τὸ δένδρον σαπρὸν καὶ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ σαπρόν ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ καρποῦ τὸ δένδρον γινώσκεται

passages.text: You brood of vipers, how can you who are evil say anything good? For out of the overflow of the heart, the mouth speaks.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
He called them a brood of vipers.
He said they were evil.
He asked how evil people could say anything good.
He explained that the mouth speaks from what fills the heart.
passages.original: γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν πῶς δύνασθε ἀγαθὰ λαλεῖν πονηροὶ ὄντες ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ περισσεύματος τῆς καρδίας τὸ στόμα λαλεῖ

passages.text: The good man brings good things out of his good store of treasure, and the evil man brings evil things out of his evil store of treasure.
passages.sermon:
A good man has a good store of treasure in his heart.
He brings out good things from this treasure.
An evil man has an evil store of treasure in his heart.
He brings out evil things from this treasure.
passages.original: ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ ἐκβάλλει ἀγαθά καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ θησαυροῦ ἐκβάλλει πονηρά

passages.text: But I tell you that men will give an account on the day of judgment for every careless word they have spoken.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said, “I tell you this truth.
God will judge every person.
God will set a day for judgment.
On that day, people must answer for every careless word they have spoken.
No careless word will be forgotten.
Each person must give an account for every word.”
passages.original: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶν ῥῆμα ἀργὸν ὃ λαλήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι ἀποδώσουσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ λόγον ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως

passages.text: For by your words you will be acquitted, and by your words you will be condemned.”
passages.sermon:
Your words have power.
Your words will decide your judgment.
Your words can acquit you.
Your words can condemn you.
passages.original: ἐκ γὰρ τῶν λόγων σου δικαιωθήσῃ καὶ ἐκ τῶν λόγων σου καταδικασθήσῃ

passages.text: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees said to Him, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from You.”
passages.sermon: Some scribes and Pharisees spoke to Jesus.\r\nThey said to Him, "Teacher, we want to see a sign from You."
passages.original: Τότε ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ τινες τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων λέγοντες Διδάσκαλε θέλομεν ἀπὸ σοῦ σημεῖον ἰδεῖν

passages.text: Jesus replied, “A wicked and adulterous generation demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the scribes and Pharisees.
He called their generation wicked and adulterous.
He said this generation demands a sign.
He said no sign will be given to it.
He said only the sign of the prophet Jonah will be given.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Γενεὰ πονηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλὶς σημεῖον ἐπιζητεῖ καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ τοῦ προφήτου

passages.text: For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
passages.sermon:
Jonah was a prophet.
Jonah stayed inside a great fish.
He was there for three days and three nights.
The Son of Man is Jesus.
Jesus will be in the heart of the earth.
He will be there for three days and three nights.
passages.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἦν Ἰωνᾶς ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ τοῦ κήτους τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ τρεῖς νύκτας οὕτως ἔσται ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ τῆς γῆς τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ τρεῖς νύκτας

passages.text: The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now One greater than Jonah is here.
passages.sermon:
The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation.
They will condemn this generation.
The men of Nineveh repented when Jonah preached to them.
Now someone greater than Jonah is here.
passages.original: Ἄνδρες Νινευῖται ἀναστήσονται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτήν ὅτι μετενόησαν εἰς τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰωνᾶ καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε

passages.text: The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and now One greater than Solomon is here.
passages.sermon:
The Queen of the South is a woman who lived far away.
She will rise at the judgment.
She will stand with this generation.
She will condemn this generation.
She came from the ends of the earth.
She traveled to hear the wisdom of Solomon.
Now someone greater than Solomon is here.
passages.original: βασίλισσα νότου ἐγερθήσεται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινεῖ αὐτήν ὅτι ἦλθεν ἐκ τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς ἀκοῦσαι τὴν σοφίαν Σολομῶνος καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Σολομῶνος ὧδε

passages.text: When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it.
passages.sermon:
An unclean spirit leaves a man.
The unclean spirit travels through dry places.
The unclean spirit looks for a place to rest.
The unclean spirit does not find rest.
passages.original: Ὅταν δὲ τὸ ἀκάθαρτον πνεῦμα ἐξέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου διέρχεται δι’ ἀνύδρων τόπων ζητοῦν ἀνάπαυσιν καὶ οὐχ εὑρίσκει

passages.text: Then it says, ‘I will return to the house I left.’ On its return, it finds the house vacant, swept clean, and put in order.
passages.sermon:
An unclean spirit leaves a person.
The spirit speaks.
It says, “I will return to my house, the place I left.”
The spirit returns to that person.
It finds the house empty.
It finds the house swept clean.
It finds the house put in order.
passages.original: τότε λέγει Εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου ἐπιστρέψω ὅθεν ἐξῆλθον καὶ ἐλθὸν εὑρίσκει σχολάζοντα καὶ σεσαρωμένον καὶ κεκοσμημένον

passages.text: Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and dwell there; and the final plight of that man is worse than the first. So will it be with this wicked generation.”
passages.sermon:
An unclean spirit leaves a man.
The unclean spirit cannot find rest.
The unclean spirit decides to return to the man.
The unclean spirit brings seven other spirits with it.
These seven spirits are more wicked than the first spirit.
All eight spirits enter the man.
All eight spirits live there.
The man's final condition becomes worse than before.
This will also happen to this wicked generation.
passages.original: τότε πορεύεται καὶ παραλαμβάνει μεθ’ ἑαυτοῦ ἑπτὰ ἕτερα πνεύματα πονηρότερα ἑαυτοῦ καὶ εἰσελθόντα κατοικεῖ ἐκεῖ καὶ γίνεται τὰ ἔσχατα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκείνου χείρονα τῶν πρώτων οὕτως ἔσται καὶ τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ τῇ πονηρᾷ

passages.text: While Jesus was still speaking to the crowds, His mother and brothers stood outside, wanting to speak to Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowds.
His mother stood outside.
His brothers stood outside.
They wanted to speak to Jesus.
passages.original: Ἔτι δὲ αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος τοῖς ὄχλοις ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ εἱστήκεισαν ἔξω ζητοῦντες αὐτῷ λαλῆσαι

passages.text: Someone told Him, “Look, Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to speak to You.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was speaking to the crowds.
Someone came to Jesus.
This person spoke to Jesus.
He said, “Look, your mother is outside.
Your brothers are also outside.
They are standing there.
They want to speak to you.”
passages.original: εἶπεν δέ τις αὐτῷ Ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου ἔξω ἑστήκασιν ζητοῦντές σοι λαλῆσαι

passages.text: But Jesus replied, “Who is My mother, and who are My brothers?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was speaking to the crowds.
Someone told Jesus that His mother and brothers were outside.
Jesus replied to the person who spoke to Him.
Jesus asked, “Who is My mother?”
Jesus also asked, “Who are My brothers?”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν τῷ λέγοντι αὐτῷ Τίς ἐστιν ἡ μήτηρ μου καὶ τίνες εἰσὶν οἱ ἀδελφοί μου

passages.text: Pointing to His disciples, He said, “Here are My mother and My brothers.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was speaking to a crowd.
His disciples were with Him.
Jesus pointed His hand toward His disciples.
He said, “Here are My mother and My brothers.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν Ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ μου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί μου

passages.text: For whoever does the will of My Father in heaven is My brother and sister and mother.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He explained who belongs to His family.
God is Jesus’ Father.
God lives in heaven.
Anyone who does the will of Jesus’ Father is part of Jesus’ family.
That person is Jesus’ brother.
That person is Jesus’ sister.
That person is Jesus’ mother.
passages.original: ὅστις γὰρ ἂν ποιήσῃ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς αὐτός μου ἀδελφὸς καὶ ἀδελφὴ καὶ μήτηρ ἐστίν
